thread.title: Canvassers make 6-point pitch for all-day referendum
thread.title_full: Canvassers make 6-point pitch for all-day referendum

author: ohtadmin
title: Canvassers make 6-point pitch for all-day referendum
text:
A proposal by the board of canvassers to reform the financial town meeting into a two-day process with an all-day referendum has been presented to the town council.
Nancy Beye, president of the council, said they would “definitely put it on a future agenda.”
Republican canvasser Hugh Murphy presented his bipartisan plan Tuesday. He said the meeting should be broken into two sections with the first part of the two-day meeting set aside for elected officials to present their budgets and listen to voters ask questions and raise concerns.
This part also is when warrants would be settled so they can be explained in detail on the ballot for an all-day referendum, which is the second part.
Murphy cited six reasons. First, “it is the duty of the canvassing authority to make recommendations and advise the town council on voter matters.”
Second, there is a “groundswell” of support from voters who want to see the meeting, which dates to Revolutionary times, modernized.
The third reason is the budget will continue to increase, which will make “exo-budgetary items, like citizen-initiated warrants, “more prevalent.”
Fourth, these bigger budgets will require other means to generate revenue, which “will provide more fodder for public debate.”
The fifth reason is the current meeting site, the gym at Lawn School, only can accommodate about 15% of the eligible voters.
The final reason is to give voters the opportunity “to truly have their say in particularly budgeting,” Murphy said.
While state law only gives the canvassing board the jurisdiction over elections, not necessarily financial town meetings, Murphy said the councilors have relied on the canvassing board to help at the FTM, which makes it akin to an election.
Examples include controlling admission into the meeting to ensure non-voters do not participate; developing and providing ballots; counting votes on ballot issues; providing the results; and operating the poll pads and voting machines.
Democratic canvasser Meredith Daphne supported Murphy’s proposal.
“To date, nobody has been turned away at the door for an FTM,” she said. “However, our preliminary research does show that when towns change their format from an FTM to an all-day referendum, voter participation does increase. That is one of the important considerations we wanted to make note of.”
Daphne also asked the councilors to include the canvassers, “as protectors of the integrity of the electoral process and voter education,” in future discussions.
Beye told the canvassers this reform is “something that can’t be done easily.” Ultimately, she said, voters need to approve an amendment to the town’s charter.
“We have a lot to think about,” she said. “I appreciate all the information you gave us. We’ll take it under advisement.”
